title: Wipro Stock Drops as Brokerages Slash Targets After Weak Q1 Results and Guidance
excerpt: Jefferies, Citi, and BofA cut price targets and retain bearish ratings after Wipro's revenue miss and soft Q2 outlook, while Nomura remains a contrarian bull on deal momentum.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Wipro's Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹24,479 crore missed estimates, with net profit rising only 0.6%.
  • Brokerages Jefferies, Citi, and BofA cut Wipro's price targets, citing disappointing performance.
  • Nomura remains bullish on Wipro, highlighting strong deal momentum and attractive dividend yield.
  • Wipro's Q2 guidance suggests revenue growth of -1.5% to +0.5%, below market expectations.

  • Wipro's Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹24,479 crore missed consensus estimates, while net profit rose just 0.6% year-on-year to ₹3,352 crore.
  • Jefferies cut its target to ₹150 from ₹180 and trimmed FY27-29 estimates by 2-5%; Citi and BofA also lowered targets with sell/underperform ratings.
  • Nomura has maintained its buy rating on Wipro, citing strong large deal bookings and an attractive dividend yield as reasons for long-term optimism.
  • Wipro guided for Q2 IT services revenue of -1.5% to +0.5% in constant currency, weaker than the street's expected range of -1% to +1%.

Wipro shares fell 2.3% on July 17 after the Bengaluru-based IT services company reported a June quarter that missed revenue and profit estimates, then issued guidance that trailed street expectations. The stock traded at ₹175.60 on the NSE, near its intraday low of ₹173.55.

The results triggered a wave of target price cuts from global brokerages, though a sharp divide persists between bears who see structural underperformance and the few bulls banking on a delayed turnaround.

What the Numbers Show

Wipro reported consolidated revenue of ₹24,479 crore ($2.54 billion) for Q1 FY27, up 10.6% year-on-year but just 1% higher sequentially. The topline missed the LSEG consensus estimate of ₹24,776 crore, according to Reuters. Net profit came in at ₹3,352 crore, edging up 0.6% from a year earlier but falling 4.2% quarter-on-quarter, undershooting the ₹3,442 crore estimate.

The core IT services segment posted revenue of $2,614.5 million, declining 1.2% sequentially in constant currency terms. Operating margin for the segment slipped to 16%, down 130 basis points from the preceding quarter and 120 basis points year-on-year. Salary hikes and the ramp-up of several large deals drove the margin compression.

Total deal wins stood at $3.37 billion, a steep drop from $5 billion a year earlier. However, large deal bookings of $1.63 billion rose 12.9% quarter-on-quarter, with 13 large deals closed during the quarter.

Jefferies maintained its underperform rating and cut its target price to ₹150 from ₹180, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. The brokerage said Wipro has struggled to deliver organic revenue growth over the past three years and that FY27 is "unlikely to be different." It trimmed FY27-FY29 revenue and profit-after-tax estimates by 2-5%, projecting a 5% earnings-per-share CAGR over that period.

Citi held its sell rating and lowered its target to ₹150 from ₹160, calling the Q1 performance "disappointing" and flagging weakness across major geographies and verticals. Bank of America retained its underperform rating with a reduced target of ₹184, down from ₹210, stating the turnaround will take longer than anticipated.

"Wipro is lagging its peers. It's possible that the type of legacy deals that Wipro has, is not able to generate sustaining growth."

— Piyush Pandey, Analyst, Centrum Broking

JPMorgan cut Wipro to underweight and slashed its ADR target to $1.70, citing AI-driven pricing pressure and weak demand. Elara Capital maintained its sell with a target of ₹160, down from ₹180, forecasting a 1% decline in dollar revenue for both FY27 and FY28. Motilal Oswal kept its neutral rating but cut its FY27 EPS estimate by about 3.5%, setting a target of ₹160.

Nomura has been the most prominent bull on Wipro, maintaining its buy rating while most peers turned negative. The Japanese brokerage has highlighted Wipro's improving large deal pipeline, a 4% FY27 dividend yield, and a valuation of roughly 20x estimated earnings as reasons the stock offers attractive upside from current levels.

In an early July note, Nomura acknowledged near-term headwinds from AI-led disruption and macroeconomic uncertainty across Indian IT services but argued the long-term addressable market will expand. It maintained positive ratings on most large-cap IT names even as it trimmed target prices across the sector, according to TradingView.

Guidance Disappoints

Wipro projected Q2 FY27 IT services revenue in the range of $2,574 million to $2,627 million, implying sequential constant currency growth of -1.5% to +0.5%. Analysts had expected a range of -1% to +1%, making the midpoint of Wipro's guidance noticeably softer.

"Clients are moving beyond technology modernisation to AI-enabled operating models that improve quality, resilience, and productivity."

— Srini Pallia, CEO and MD, Wipro

CFO Aparna Iyer warned of "near-term margin volatility" as the company invests in employees and strategic growth areas. She noted that including the ₹2 per share interim dividend declared by the board, Wipro has returned more than $3 billion in cash to shareholders over the past year.

Wider IT Sector Context

Wipro's struggles stand out against its larger peers. Rivals TCS, HCLTech, and Tech Mahindra all beat quarterly revenue expectations, aided by a depreciating rupee and strength in certain segments, according to Reuters. The divergence has reinforced Wipro's reputation as the weakest performer among India's top four IT exporters.

The Americas market, Wipro's largest geography, declined due to client-specific issues and technology spending cuts in healthcare, CEO Pallia said without elaborating. Voluntary attrition stood at 13.9% on a trailing 12-month basis, and headcount was 243,044 as of June 30.

What Comes Next

Wipro's Q2 Revenue Guidance
›Projected revenue range: $2,574M to $2,627M
›Expected growth: -1.5% to +0.5%
›Market expected range: -1% to +1%
›Midpoint of guidance is softer than expectations.

Of 38 analysts covering Wipro, only six have buy or outperform ratings, while 17 hold and 17 recommend selling, according to FT data as of July 17. The median 12-month target of ₹175 implies virtually no upside from the current price, with the range spanning ₹150 to ₹226.

The next earnings announcement is expected on October 13. Until then, investors will watch whether large deal ramp-ups begin translating into organic revenue growth — the missing ingredient that separates Nomura's thesis from the bearish majority.
